Record what is paused, why, who authorised it, what is needed for review and the next review date. Keep evidence and fund records intact.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Review freezing and closure > Temporary restriction
metadata.heading_path: Review freezing and closure > Temporary restriction

content:
## Inactive collectives

Decision confirmed by JF on 14 September 2026. Both conditions must be met:

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Review freezing and closure > Inactive collectives
metadata.heading_path: Review freezing and closure > Inactive collectives

content:
Document the transaction history and the communication attempts, then send a final request for a response. If the collective remains unresponsive, initiate termination with 30 days' written notice in accordance with the applicable hosting agreement and its notice provisions. Inactivity alone does not automatically freeze the collective or reallocate its funds.

Handle any remaining balance, outstanding expenses and other assets under the applicable termination provisions, subject to applicable law and any required third-party approvals. Retain the final contact attempt, termination notice, decision and resulting records.

This process concerns an identified collective. Unidentified incoming funds follow the separate procedure linked below. The [published hosting template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/e/2PACX-1vS2jTb55T-kXHDPLNWVg4xUuMGmediT9VBqwsNpdQA8geRpcPsyYvfPggwJ6iZaPw/pub) reviewed on 24 September 2026 includes the matching inactivity provision. Before applying it to an existing initiative, check its applicable agreement, effective date and any required notification or approval.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Review freezing and closure
metadata.heading_path: Review freezing and closure > Inactive collectives

content:
## Closure and remaining funds

Do not treat retention, reallocation or closure without transfer as an ordinary automatic outcome. The consolidated audit requires a contractual or legal basis and formal decision for these actions. A platform control does not supply that authority.

Record outstanding agreements, expenses, reports and the authorised treatment of remaining funds before closing the case. For unidentified money, use [the separate holding process](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/unclaimed-or-unreconciliable-funds).

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Review freezing and closure > Closure and remaining funds
metadata.heading_path: Review freezing and closure > Closure and remaining funds

content:
## Source and review

Operational update: 14 September 2026. JF confirmed the cumulative inactivity criteria and final-contact/30-day termination process above. This resolves that operational decision in audit V05; it does not establish specialist validation of every freezing or closure scenario.

metadata.heading_path: Review freezing and closure > Source and review

# Review an initiative

Document mission, structure, people and funding before a decision.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Review an initiative
metadata.heading_path: Review an initiative

content:
## Trigger and inputs

Use this review for a new application or a material change to an existing initiative. Gather the application, public profile, legal status if any, team information, activities, geography, budget and expected funding sources.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Review an initiative > Trigger and inputs
metadata.heading_path: Review an initiative > Trigger and inputs

content: There is no automatic Europe-only eligibility limit for OCE Foundation. A lack of incorporation does not itself make an initiative unsuitable; use [the informal-group review](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/due-diligence-for-unregistered-groups).

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Review an initiative
metadata.heading_path: Review an initiative > Standard review

content:
## Enhanced review

Additional checks may be needed where the activity, jurisdiction, funder, payment route or conflicting information creates a material concern. Identify the actual concern and proportionate evidence needed. Seek specialist advice when the issue is legal or financial.

Do not equate a sensitive context or a limited public presence with wrongdoing. Consider whether publicity itself creates a safety risk.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Review an initiative > Enhanced review
metadata.heading_path: Review an initiative > Enhanced review

content:

Record the evidence checked, findings, unresolved questions, recommendation, decision-maker and decision date in the restricted case record. Keep personal documents in Drive or the appropriate restricted system, not in a general handbook page.

Use [risk and escalation](/oc-europe-internal-doc/risk-and-compliance) for unresolved concerns and [application review](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/application-review) for the workflow.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Review an initiative > Output and decision
metadata.heading_path: Review an initiative > Output and decision

content:

Checked on 24 September 2026. First triage and operational responsibilities (A01) and the administrator rule (A02) were adopted on 14 September. metadata.heading_path: Review an initiative > Source and review

# Review an informal or unregistered group

Adapt the evidence to the group while keeping its people and funds accountable.

Informal groups are part of OCE’s mission. This is the reference page for their review; the former parallel handling page now points here.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Review an informal or unregistered group
metadata.heading_path: Review an informal or unregistered group

content: Verify identity through the appropriate private process. Do not require a legal name or identity document to be public merely because OCE needs to verify it.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Review an informal or unregistered group
metadata.heading_path: Review an informal or unregistered group > Understand the group

content:
## Where evidence is difficult to obtain

Ask for a short explanation, relevant links, a conversation or other appropriate corroboration. Record why a particular document cannot be provided and what remains uncertain. An alternative must be assessed rather than invented by the reviewer.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Review an informal or unregistered group > Where evidence is difficult to obtain
metadata.heading_path: Review an informal or unregistered group > Where evidence is difficult to obtain

content:
## Funding and payment route

Do not automatically route a group to OSE, require incorporation or reject it solely because it expects a substantial grant. Establish the actual legal and operational arrangement with the competent reviewers.

If the grantee and the proposed payee differ, pause the affected payment and obtain a documented decision on that route. See [grant lifecycle](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures).

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Review an informal or unregistered group > Funding and payment route
metadata.heading_path: Review an informal or unregistered group > Funding and payment route

content:

The [administrator rule](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/application-review#administrator-minimum) sets two active administrators as the default and allows a documented exception for a genuinely individual project. Assess responsibility, continuity and OCE’s usual pre-payment checks of the administrator’s expenses; record the exception in J1-05 with its reason, decision-maker and review conditions.

The sole administrator may submit and approve their own expense. OCE checks the supporting documents, connection to the project and applicable funding conditions before payment.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Review an informal or unregistered group > Administrator minimum
metadata.heading_path: Review an informal or unregistered group > Administrator minimum

The organisation checklist and documented exceptional personal-account/intermediary routes were confirmed on 14 September 2026 in [the grant lifecycle](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures). metadata.heading_path: Review an informal or unregistered group > Open policy points

Checked on 24 September 2026 against the decisions of 14 September: administrator exception A02 and the operational onward-grant checklist. content:
# Manage the grant lifecycle

Take a grant from announcement to evidenced receipt, delivery and closure.

#### Purpose and responsibilities

Use this procedure when a collective announces funding it expects to receive through OCE, usually by email. The collective introduces OCE to the donor foundation; Laura coordinates the contract and transfer arrangements with the foundation.

**Laura owns the grant file and this procedure.** She reviews funding conditions before OCE commits, coordinates the agreements, tracks obligations and follows the dossier through to closure.

**Ivan prepares the operational receipt and allocation, maintains transaction evidence and executes authorised operations. CFO retains financial review and conclusions.** The collective supplies project information and delivers its agreed activities and reporting contributions.

Use the [operational RACI](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/raci-operationnelle) for decision routes. File ownership does not confer signing authority. JF handles material commitments and genuine exceptions; reserved matters follow the applicable governance route.

#### At a glance

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Manage the grant lifecycle > Purpose and responsibilities
metadata.heading_path: Manage the grant lifecycle

content:
#### 1. Qualify the arrangement

Create or update the grant’s record in OCE Grants as soon as the collective announces the funding. Laura ensures that the record exists and has a named owner. Capture the collective and platform link, donor foundation and contact, expected amount and currency, purpose, timetable and next action. Obtain the introduction to the foundation and link the relevant correspondence.

Identify the legal recipient, beneficiary and intended activities. Confirm whether OCE is receiving a grant, administering a fund or processing an onward grant. Do not infer the legal model from a platform profile.

Use [Forms of support and administrative contributions](/oc-europe-internal-doc/the-foundation/forms-of-support-and-administrative-contributions) to identify the support arrangement, scope and contribution calculation. Funding routes can cross the support models; the applicable agreement determines the obligations.

**Ready for review:** the parties and intended funding route are identified, with missing information assigned to an owner.

For public funding or a nonstandard structure, obtain the appropriate case decision. For Ma Earth, use the actual upstream agreement and legal review; definitive legal characterisation remains unresolved.

#### 2. Review documents and authority

**Review the funder’s conditions**

Laura gathers the proposal, budget, funding conditions, due-diligence material and draft agreement. Identify:

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Manage the grant lifecycle > 1. Qualify the arrangement
metadata.heading_path: Manage the grant lifecycle > 1. Qualify the arrangement

content:
The CFO reviews financial questions within his role. Laura obtains the appropriate decision on unresolved commitments or specialist issues. Record the answer, decision-maker and supporting reference; a conversation alone does not establish that a condition is resolved.

**Prepare coherent agreements**

Check that the agreement with the foundation and the mandate with the collective describe compatible purposes, obligations, timelines and financial terms. A mandate is required for collectives receiving grants through OCE. Follow [agreement preparation](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures/creation-and-sending-of-mandate-agreements) for templates, checks, signature and storage.

Identify the authorised signatories and obtain the applicable approvals. Link the signed versions in the restricted grant record.

**Ready for commitment:** relevant conditions have been reviewed and required decisions are recorded. A draft or a sent signature request is not a signed agreement. Keep unresolved items visible and pause the affected commitment or action; continue unaffected preparation.

#### 3. Track the grant

**Every grant must be registered in OCE Grants.** It is the operational reference for the grant’s follow-up, deadlines and next actions. Laura ensures registration and keeps the record current throughout the grant lifecycle.

Record each reporting deadline, project end date and other contractual deadline, with the person responsible for the action. Add expected payment dates and the next action where known. If a date is not yet known, record the missing information and who will obtain it; do not invent a deadline.

Update the record when an agreement is signed or amended, a payment is received, a report is submitted or an obligation is completed. Keep submission evidence linked, and track remaining obligations until closure. For Myriad requests, also follow [Coordinate Myriad USA](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures/myriad-usa).

Use Open Collective for collective, fund and transaction records, and restricted Drive folders for signed agreements and supporting evidence. Link these records from OCE Grants rather than creating a competing grant register. See [Tools and records — grant tracking](/oc-europe-internal-doc/tools-and-platforms-used-at-oce#grant-tracking-next-cycle-delivery).

Use the control sheet below within the OCE Grants dossier. If a dedicated field is unavailable, link a restricted note from that dossier. This procedure does not presume that every checklist item has a dedicated application field or that automatic reminders are configured.

**Prepare the transfer and hand over to Ivan**

Laura coordinates the transfer arrangements with the foundation. Before the expected transfer, give Ivan:

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Manage the grant lifecycle > 3. Track the grant
metadata.heading_path: Manage the grant lifecycle > 2. Review documents and authority

content:
Ivan checks that the information is sufficient to recognise and allocate the receipt and flags missing operational details to Laura. Laura keeps ownership of funder questions. CFO reviews financial uncertainty where needed.

**Ready for transfer:** the required agreement and conditions are in place, the destination and matching information are clear, and the operational handover is recorded. If funds arrive unexpectedly, record the receipt and resolve missing information before treating the grant as ready for allocation or use.

**Grant control sheet**

For each line, record **complete, pending or not applicable**, with the evidence link, owner and next action/date where needed. Explain why a line is not applicable. These are checklist values, not presumed software statuses.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Manage the grant lifecycle
metadata.heading_path: Manage the grant lifecycle > 3. Track the grant

content:
The checklist records the evidence; it does not replace the agreements or confer approval.

#### 4. Receive and allocate

Ivan matches the actual bank receipt to the agreement, expected transfer and platform record. Check the payer/reference, amount, currency and tranche. Record discrepancies such as a partial receipt, unexpected charges or an unidentified transfer, and route them to Laura or CFO as appropriate. Do not mark an expected receipt as received solely because the donor says it has been sent.

Follow [Incoming transfers](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/bank-transfers-for-the-collectives) and its [grant receipt checklist](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/bank-transfers-for-the-collectives#grant-receipt-checklist-net-allocation-and-administrative-contribution): verify the signed mandate’s contribution terms, credit the collective net, manually record the administrative contribution on the correct operating budget, and link and reconcile both entries without an additional automatic platform fee.

Ivan retains the transaction references and evidence. Laura ensures the collective is informed of the actual receipt and allocation, including any unresolved issue or restriction. CFO retains financial review; operational entry alone is not an independent financial conclusion.

**Receipt complete:** the actual funds are matched, allocation is evidenced, discrepancies are resolved or explicitly tracked, and the collective has been informed. Receipt does not remove restrictions on use.

#### 5. Review onward payments

For an onward grant to an organisation, retain:

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Manage the grant lifecycle > 4. Receive and allocate
metadata.heading_path: Manage the grant lifecycle > 3. Track the grant

content:
**Exceptional situations — internal handling**

Where there is no legal organisation, payment may exceptionally be made directly to an individual's account. Document the absence of a legal structure, the beneficiary and project, the individual's identity and role, account ownership, purpose, applicable agreement and the case decision. Record why standard organisation documents cannot be provided and the evidence supporting the arrangement.

Payment may also be made through an intermediary. In addition to the beneficiary/project documentation, collect the intermediary's bank account evidence and all applicable supporting documents for the intermediary, including its identity or registration, representative authority and agreement establishing its role. Document the relationship between beneficiary and intermediary and the intended transfer and use of funds.

Keep personal and banking evidence in restricted records and retain the payment trail. These exceptional routes require a documented case; they do not determine the separate Organisation/Vendor platform-profile question, which remains deferred.

#### 6. Report and close

Laura records each obligation in OCE Grants with its owner and deadline. Coordinate narrative reporting with the collective/project owner and financial information with CFO; Ivan supplies transaction evidence. Link submitted reports and submission confirmations. Retain acceptance evidence where the agreement requires it.

Record amendments and changes to dates, budget or conditions in the same dossier. Update the relevant obligations and inform those implementing the change.

Before closing, Laura checks that:

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Manage the grant lifecycle > 6. Report and close
metadata.heading_path: Manage the grant lifecycle > 5. Review onward payments

content:
**A transfer or a submitted report alone does not close the grant.** Keep the dossier open where a required action remains.

#### Maintain this procedure

Laura keeps this procedure aligned with the operating process, with Ivan for operational steps and CFO for financial controls. Review the affected guidance when a funding route, contractual requirement, tool or responsibility changes, or when a recurring error exposes a gap. Use [Review operational records](/oc-europe-internal-doc/tools-and-platforms-used-at-oce/oce-periodic-cleanup) to identify outstanding work and outdated guidance.

Keep this public page focused on the process. Store agreements, personal or banking information and case evidence in restricted records.

Specialist legal/tax validation, contract-specific characterisation and the Organisation/Vendor question remain separate matters tracked in [documentation decisions and remaining validations](/oc-europe-internal-doc/tools-and-platforms-used-at-oce/brand).

See [U.S. funding](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures/receiving-funds-from-the-u.s.), [Myriad USA](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures/myriad-usa) and [GSF](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures/gsf) for route-specific workflows.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Manage the grant lifecycle > Maintain this procedure
metadata.heading_path: Manage the grant lifecycle > 6. Report and close

content:
# Choose a U.S. funding route

Distinguish direct foundation grants from the Myriad donation route.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Choose a U.S. funding route
metadata.heading_path: Choose a U.S. funding route

content:
## Confirm the entity first

OCEF and OSE are separate legal entities. Do not use one entity’s agreement, account or eligibility documentation for the other.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Choose a U.S. funding route > Confirm the entity first
metadata.heading_path: Choose a U.S. funding route > Confirm the entity first

content:
## U.S. private foundation

Check whether the funder can use OCE’s current Equivalency Determination documentation. Obtain the current evidence and confirm that it applies to the intended grant. The existence of an ED is not an automatic approval for every foundation or grant.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Choose a U.S. funding route > U.S. private foundation
metadata.heading_path: Choose a U.S. funding route > U.S. private foundation

content:
## Myriad USA

For an eligible arrangement using Myriad, Laura coordinates the operational relationship, grant request and reporting. Follow [the Myriad procedure](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures/myriad-usa). Do not ask collectives to manage the Myriad relationship directly.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Choose a U.S. funding route > Myriad USA
metadata.heading_path: Choose a U.S. funding route > Myriad USA

content:
## Direct contribution

A direct contribution to the platform or OCE account does not, by itself, establish U.S. tax deductibility. Confirm the intended route before instructions are sent.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Choose a U.S. funding route > Direct contribution
metadata.heading_path: Choose a U.S. funding route > Direct contribution

content:
## OSE status to check

The reviewed email thread confirms that OSE needs its own application and agreement with Myriad. Laura’s 7 September message asks whether setup should remain on hold. No later approval is established by that thread. Do not document the OSE route as active or automatically move a collective to OCEF to obtain it.

For every route, retain the agreement, entity, receipt, allocation and reporting evidence.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Choose a U.S. funding route > OSE status to check
metadata.heading_path: Choose a U.S. funding route > OSE status to check

content:

Editorial review: 11 September 2026. The [consolidated audit](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1L-xi_oBqx5osXoe_jaa4TXNSx-oZtYqA/edit) identifies V13 as requiring a decision or specialist validation. This rewrite does not adopt those proposals. Record the approved text and effective date before changing the corresponding operating rule. [Myriad agreement thread](https://mail.google.com/mail/#all/1a0490ca968e5597), latest reviewed message 7 September 2026.

metadata.heading_path: Choose a U.S. funding route > Source and review

# Receive European funding

Check the funder’s conditions and the applicable legal arrangement.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Receive European funding
metadata.heading_path: Receive European funding

content:
## Qualify the opportunity

Identify the funder, intended activity, legal recipient, amount, currency and deadline. Check whether the funder accepts the proposed hosted arrangement. For public funding, apply the case-by-case decision route below.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Receive European funding > Qualify the opportunity
metadata.heading_path: Receive European funding > Qualify the opportunity

content:
## Public funding

OCE has not yet accepted public funding. Public funding remains an exploratory opportunity for hosted collectives and for OCE itself, with previous exploration involving Open Source Europe. Assess each opportunity individually; this is not an established service or a blanket eligibility commitment. JF gives the go-ahead before OCE commits to a case. Review the funder’s conditions and the applicable legal arrangement for that opportunity.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Receive European funding > Public funding
metadata.heading_path: Receive European funding > Public funding

content:
## Agreement and receipt

Review the agreement before commitment. Verify the signatory’s authority and any required mandate. Provide the correct receiving instructions, retain the signed documents and follow [receipt and allocation](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/bank-transfers-for-the-collectives).

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Receive European funding > Agreement and receipt
metadata.heading_path: Receive European funding > Agreement and receipt

content:
## Tax statements

JF confirmed on 14 September 2026 that European tax-deductible donation arrangements are exceptional, assessed on request for substantial amounts. No numeric threshold has been established in this decision. Assess the country and available route before providing donation instructions or tax assurances. The U.S. donation route is Myriad USA, subject to that route's conditions and the donor's tax circumstances; citizenship or payment origin alone does not establish deductibility.

Do not infer country-specific deductibility from OCE’s public utility status or an ecosystem partnership. The audit explicitly suspends the old blanket KBF recognition claim. Obtain the competent tax or legal confirmation before making such a statement.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Receive European funding > Tax statements
metadata.heading_path: Receive European funding > Tax statements

content:
## Follow-up

Track purpose restrictions, reporting dates and changes in the project record. Coordinate financial information through the agreed financial-control route.

Return to **Manage the grant lifecycle** in the navigation for the common checklist.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Receive European funding > Follow-up
metadata.heading_path: Receive European funding > Follow-up

content:
## Source and review

Editorial review: 11 September 2026. The [consolidated audit](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1L-xi_oBqx5osXoe_jaa4TXNSx-oZtYqA/edit) identified A04, A09 and V07. The mandate scope A04 and the public-funding decision route A09 were confirmed on 14 September 2026. V07 tax validation remains separate. Record the approved text and effective date before changing the corresponding operating rule.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Receive European funding > Source and review
metadata.heading_path: Receive European funding > Source and review

content:
# Prepare a mandate agreement

Use the correct approved template, verify authority and retain the signed record.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Prepare a mandate agreement
metadata.heading_path: Prepare a mandate agreement

content:
## Before drafting

Confirm why a mandate is needed for this arrangement, the legal entity, the activity and the approved template. Apply the funding-based scope confirmed below.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Prepare a mandate agreement > Before drafting
metadata.heading_path: Prepare a mandate agreement > Before drafting

content:
## When a mandate is required

A mandate agreement is mandatory for collectives receiving grants through OCE. It is optional for collectives receiving only crowdfunding donations without particular conditions. Review other funding arrangements, including contributions with particular conditions, case by case to determine the appropriate agreement. The general hosting terms remain applicable when a mandate is optional.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Prepare a mandate agreement > When a mandate is required
metadata.heading_path: Prepare a mandate agreement > When a mandate is required

content:
## Controls

Do not rewrite legal clauses from memory. Do not assume that two names, a particular end-date setting or a historical Board list is correct for every agreement. Check the actual mandate and delegation.

Screen relevant parties through the established review process and resolve material questions before signature. Keep identity evidence and signatures out of public pages.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Prepare a mandate agreement > Controls
metadata.heading_path: Prepare a mandate agreement > Controls

content:
## Completion

The record should contain the approved version, signatures, date, applicable entity and link to the platform record. A sent signature request is not a completed agreement.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Prepare a mandate agreement > Completion
metadata.heading_path: Prepare a mandate agreement > Completion

content:
## Source and review

Editorial review: 11 September 2026. The [consolidated audit](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1L-xi_oBqx5osXoe_jaa4TXNSx-oZtYqA/edit) identified A04, A02 and V10 for decision or specialist validation. The funding-based scope of A04 was confirmed on 14 September 2026 above; A02 is recorded in the administrator rule. Specialist validation of the mandate template and signing authority remains separate.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Prepare a mandate agreement > Source and review
metadata.heading_path: Prepare a mandate agreement > Source and review

content:
# Coordinate Myriad USA

Track the grant request, allocation and reporting as one cycle.

**Operational coordination: Laura.** OCE manages the relationship with Myriad; collectives and beneficiaries do not contact Myriad directly under the documented workflow.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Coordinate Myriad USA
metadata.heading_path: Coordinate Myriad USA

content:
## Before a request

Confirm the OCE legal entity, eligible project, intended route and applicable agreement. Verify the current contact and individual portal access. Do not store access codes or authentication links in this handbook.

JF confirmed on 7 October 2026 that the initial agreement signed with Myriad covers subsequent requests. The agreement is retained in the Myriad USA folder in Drive. Refer to that existing agreement when preparing a request, alongside the request-specific purpose, conditions and reporting requirements. This confirmation concerns the agreement with Myriad; it does not settle the documentation or approval of an onward transfer to another legal entity.

Use the **Grants Portal** to submit regranting requests from Myriad USA to OCE, and the **Fund Portal** to manage and monitor the Myriad fund. Their links and uses are set out below. The **Donor Portal** serves donor activity; it is a separate route.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Coordinate Myriad USA > Before a request
metadata.heading_path: Coordinate Myriad USA > Before a request

# Plan the finance cycle

Keep recurring work visible without maintaining conflicting calendars.

#### During the week

Review incoming transfers, liquidity by entity and currency, ready-to-pay requests, incomplete expenses, failed payments, support cases and provider disputes. Track expected grants with the project owner.

Plan transfers needed to fund payout accounts before execution. USD movements can require additional lead time; use current bank instructions and observed status rather than a guaranteed arrival time.

#### Payment sessions

OCE executes a submitted expense within seven business days after it has been approved by a collective administrator. This timeframe concerns execution by OCE, not receipt of the funds in the beneficiary’s bank account.

A problem preventing payment, such as missing documentation or an inconsistency requiring resolution, may extend this timeframe. Inform the requester of the blocking issue and the information or action needed to resolve it.

Monday and Thursday are the usual historical processing days. They are an internal working rhythm, not a guarantee of payment on a particular weekday; the seven-business-day rule is the reference.

#### Monthly

**By the 25th of each month at the latest:** Ivan completes salary processing through SD Worx and meal-voucher processing through Edenred (€10 face value per voucher), planning earlier where necessary so salaries are received before month-end. Verify submission and payment/order status; escalate any threatened deadline to JF. Follow the [payroll and meal-voucher procedure](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/payroll-expense-processing).

Prepare bank/platform evidence and the unresolved-item list for financial review. Check grant allocations, reporting deadlines and, for the applicable host, GitHub Sponsors allocation reports. Reuse the existing finance meeting and records.

#### Quarterly

Prepare [accounting records](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/quarterly-accounting), review outstanding reconciliation items and confirm the period-close instructions with the CFO and accountant.

#### Handover

Each open item needs an owner, next action and date. Before absence, verify the backup’s authority and access. Do not rely on a static statement that someone can always take over.

The professionalisation plan’s financial pack and continuity test remain separate deliverables requiring evidence.

#### Source and review

Editorial review: 11 September 2026. The [consolidated audit](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1L-xi_oBqx5osXoe_jaa4TXNSx-oZtYqA/edit) identifies A03, V01 and V11. JF confirmed A03 on 14 September 2026 as recorded in Payment sessions. V01 and V11 remain subject to their respective validations. # Match incoming bank transfers

Record the actual receipt against the correct entity, currency and collective.

#### Inputs

Use [Forms of support and administrative contributions](/oc-europe-internal-doc/the-foundation/forms-of-support-and-administrative-contributions) for the funding classification, default calculation base, costs and cancellation rules approved on 19 October 2026. Particular agreements and valid amendments remain applicable; resolve conflicting terms before allocation. The two manual grant entries below remain required.

Use the bank transaction, contribution order or grant reference, intended collective and supporting correspondence. Check whether the receipt is already represented by an automated platform entry before adding funds.

#### Match an existing contribution

In the host dashboard’s bank-sync workflow, locate the bank transaction and matching contribution. Compare reference, amount, currency and recipient before using **Match**.

#### Allocate an identifiable receipt without an order

For a grant or other identifiable receipt, use the supported **Add Funds** route after checking the agreement and actual bank receipt. Record the reference and a short internal explanation. Verify the resulting entry and avoid duplicating an existing allocation.

**Grant receipt checklist: net allocation and administrative contribution**

**Owner:** Ivan is responsible and accountable for allocating an identified receipt under [RACI line 26](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/raci-operationnelle). Laura supplies or clarifies the grant purpose, conditions and dossier and organises an authorised replacement when needed. CFO handles financial discrepancies and reconciliation review. Routine allocation within the agreed terms does not require a new prior approval from CFO or JF.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Match incoming bank transfers > Inputs
metadata.heading_path: Match incoming bank transfers

content:
If one entry succeeds and the other fails or its result is uncertain, record that partial state and inspect the platform history before retrying. Complete or correct only the missing/incorrect entry through the supported route, keeping the audit trail; do not repeat both entries.

For a missing agreement, beneficiary or funding-condition question, contact Laura. For a calculation, fee-currency, cost-allocation or reconciliation discrepancy, contact CFO. A new contribution exception or material departure goes to JF under the existing RACI. Record the blocker, owner and next action; no new fee rate, monetary threshold or blanket approval requirement is created by this checklist.

#### Resolve discrepancies

Do not assume that a receipt in an EUR account belongs to an EUR collective, or that an expected amount equals the amount received. Record the actual movement, apply the currency rule below and obtain the appropriate decision for any other unusual route before finalising.

The legacy pages cite Zoho and platform Bank Sync inconsistently. Confirm the current workflow with the financial owner before changing the official accounting or reconciliation record.

#### Currency conversion

When incoming funds are in a different currency from the collective, execute an actual conversion into the collective’s currency when processing the receipt, in either direction, including USD to EUR and EUR to USD. Credit the collective with the net amount actually obtained from the executed conversion, not a notional amount calculated from an indicative daily rate. The collective bears the conversion costs included in that operation; do not deduct those same costs a second time. Retain the conversion evidence, including the date, applied rate, source amount and net amount received.

It does not replace the separate work on the Foundation’s wider foreign-exchange risk policy.

#### Unidentified receipts

Search the order, correspondence and existing project records. If the destination remains unclear, follow hold and investigate funds. Do not treat elapsed time as authority for reallocation.

#### Completion evidence

Keep the bank reference, platform entry, collective, currency, review and any correction linked. Verify the credited balance and donor visibility setting.

#### Source and review

Grant-allocation checklist clarified at JF's request on 19 October 2026: signed mandate verification, net collective allocation and separate manual administrative contribution to the operating budget. Existing RACI, contract terms and approved currency rule remain applicable.

Editorial review: 11 September 2026. The [consolidated audit](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1L-xi_oBqx5osXoe_jaa4TXNSx-oZtYqA/edit) identifies A08, V03 and V11. The A08 incoming-funds conversion rule was approved on 14 September 2026 above. V03 and V11 remain subject to their respective validations. The existing internal procedure records Belgian payroll administration through SD Worx. Confirm the current employment arrangement and access before handling a payroll task.

#### Payroll preparation

JF supplies or approves payroll inputs and any changes to employment terms or remuneration. **Ivan is responsible for the monthly operational processing and submission of salaries through SD Worx**, using the approved inputs and authorised payment process.

#### Monthly deadline: no later than the 25th

**Ivan must complete salary processing through SD Worx and meal-voucher processing through Edenred no later than the 25th of each month.** The objective is for employees to receive their salaries before the end of the month. Plan earlier when provider/bank processing times or non-working days require it; the 25th is the latest internal deadline, not the day to start preparation.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Process payroll and meal vouchers > Payroll preparation
metadata.heading_path: Process payroll and meal vouchers

content:
#### Absence coverage

Before planned leave affecting this monthly cycle, Ivan must hand over the SD Worx and Edenred tasks to an explicitly designated, authorised backup with verified individual access, approved inputs and clear deadlines. Naming someone as backup does not itself grant access or authority. The proposed role-backup policy remains subject to adoption.

#### Platform record

Ivan records the monthly operational payroll expense using the appropriate summary and allocation. Match it to the payroll evidence and confirmed payment, and avoid duplicate entries.

#### Privacy

Keep individual payslips, salary details and personal identifiers in restricted HR records. Use a neutral public title if an aggregated platform entry is required. Do not assume an expense is private merely because it is an internal operating cost.

#### Period-end

Use [quarterly accounting records](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/quarterly-accounting) for the SD Worx evidence needed for the period. Resolve accounting treatment through the competent financial and payroll contacts.

# Handle refunds and disputes

Verify the original transaction, authority and provider status before acting.

#### Intake

Identify the transaction, requester, collective, entity, amount, currency and reason. Check whether a provider dispute is already open and record its actual deadline.

#### Review

Gather the original contribution, payment evidence and relevant correspondence. Confirm the applicable agreement and current provider options. Do not issue a blanket legal statement that every donation is non-refundable.

#### Decision

All OCE team members are authorised to approve and carry out refunds to donors. Prior approval from CFO or JF is not required. This authority does not remove the transaction checks and recording requirements below. Escalate material, repeated or suspected-fraud cases appropriately.

#### Execute and record

Use the approved refund route and check for an existing refund or disputed transaction first. Avoid a separate payment that could duplicate a provider refund or chargeback. Record the reference, actual outcome and the effect on the platform and bank records.

#### Provider-specific follow-up

Assemble period evidence and obtain the financial review before closure.

#### Scope

Prepare evidence for OCEF EUR and USD, distinguishing Foundation operating activity, hosted collectives and internal funds such as GSF. Platform categories do not themselves determine the legal or tax treatment.

#### Responsibility and VAT follow-up

Ivan owns the collection and preparation of accounting documents, including supporting records for operational expenses charged to OCEF budgets. He follows up on missing pieces and makes the accounting pack available to Saïd, keeping the CFO informed.

For each VAT period, Ivan follows the process through to completion:

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Prepare quarterly accounting records > Scope

content:
Saïd remains responsible for accounting work and returns within his engagement. The CFO reviews the supporting evidence and outstanding issues and coordinates accounting instructions and conclusions. Ivan escalates missing confirmations, unclear instructions or a deadline at risk to the CFO; if the CFO is unavailable, escalate to JF so that follow-up is assigned.

#### Documents to assemble

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Prepare quarterly accounting records > Documents to assemble
metadata.heading_path: Prepare quarterly accounting records > Responsibility and VAT follow-up

content:
#### File preparation

Use the [existing accounting folder](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XTFPtsXH0rhCvyzbuEFkeiSV6zCGUzxa). Keep one invoice per item and avoid combined PDFs that obscure individual documents. Store invoices in the appropriate Bills section and statements/exports in the period’s bank and platform reports.

For internal card expenses, check that the document names the Foundation where required. Do not apply the standard hosted-collective invoice addressee to OCE’s own operating activity.

#### Review

Match the period, accounts, totals and supporting records. Keep unresolved items visible for the financial reviewer. CFO owns financial review and coordination with Saïd; obtain and retain the applicable review before describing the period as closed.

#### Late documents and corrections

Do not silently change a closed folder or decide a new accounting period for a late invoice. Preserve the original document date, record when it was received and obtain the accountant’s treatment through the agreed route. Keep any correction traceable.

Retain the prepared pack, review findings, corrections or reservations, and dated closure/filing confirmation as applicable. Preparation of accounts and governance approval are separate events.

Match the transaction to the platform contribution and collective. Gather the relevant record, contribution description and correspondence. Explain the transaction accurately without adding claims that the evidence does not support.

Save the submitted evidence and confirmation. Track the provider’s decision and any bank or balance movement. Update the support record and reconciliation evidence without duplicating the transaction.

content:
## Internal 24-month rule

Operational decision confirmed by JF on 14 September 2026: after 24 months, carry out a final search for the intended beneficiary. If the beneficiary remains unidentified after that final search, apply the reallocation procedure below for Open Collective Europe's operating budget, subject to the applicable agreement, law, funding restrictions and required approvals.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Hold and investigate unidentified funds > Internal 24-month rule
metadata.heading_path: Hold and investigate unidentified funds > Internal 24-month rule

content:
## Investigate and track

Check platform orders, bank references, grant records and relevant correspondence. Where appropriate, ask the likely donor or collective for evidence through a private channel. Keep received funds distinguishable from available operating money while investigation is ongoing.

Record the receipt date, amount, currency, account, reference, research performed, owner and next review action. Document the final search and its outcome before recording any reallocation. Retain the receipt, decision and resulting platform and accounting entries. If the intended collective is identified, verify and record the correct allocation.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Hold and investigate unidentified funds > Investigate and track
metadata.heading_path: Hold and investigate unidentified funds > Investigate and track

The [published hosting template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/e/2PACX-1vS2jTb55T-kXHDPLNWVg4xUuMGmediT9VBqwsNpdQA8geRpcPsyYvfPggwJ6iZaPw/pub) reviewed on 24 September 2026 contains an explicit unidentified-contributions provision: 24 months from receipt, a documented final search and possible reallocation to the Foundation’s general operating budget if the beneficiary remains unidentified, subject to applicable law, donor restrictions and required third-party approvals.

It separately addresses identified inactive initiatives and their termination procedure. Do not apply the unidentified-contributions rule to a known collective’s remaining balance. Before relying on a new provision for an existing arrangement, check the applicable version, notification and effective-date requirements. Presence in the published template is not proof of legal validation or notification to every existing initiative.

Describe the actual concern, protect the evidence and obtain the right decision.

#### When to use this process

Use it when an application, transaction, agreement or new fact creates an unresolved legal, financial, safeguarding or reputational concern.

#### Prepare the review

Record the facts, source dates, affected entity and activity, potential impact, missing evidence, options and the decision needed. Separate an allegation from a verified finding.

Use relevant official sources and specialist advice for legal or sanctions questions. A screening result requires examination; a name match alone is not a final conclusion.

content:

Pause the affected commitment or payment if its basis is unresolved. Continue unaffected information gathering and record the next action. Do not treat a high amount, a redirection or an incomplete file alone as a nonstandard exception.

Retain the decision, authority, reasons, scope, conditions and review date. # Environmental commitments

Practical measures for OCE operations and relevant grant activities.

**Approved by:** Executive Director **Review cycle:** Annual, or earlier following a material change in activities or applicable requirements

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Environmental commitments
metadata.heading_path: Environmental commitments

content:
## Purpose

Open Collective Europe Foundation (“OCE”) recognises that responsible grant-making and organisational management include limiting negative environmental impacts and supporting sustainable development. This policy establishes the environmental principles and practices applicable to OCE’s own operations and, where relevant and proportionate, to the grant-making and re-granting programmes it administers.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Environmental commitments > Purpose
metadata.heading_path: Environmental commitments > Purpose

content:
## Scope

This policy applies to OCE employees, contractors and operational activities under OCE’s direct control. Hosted collectives and grantees remain responsible for their own operations and compliance, but OCE may incorporate proportionate environmental considerations into due diligence, contracting and monitoring where relevant to the funded activity or donor requirements.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Environmental commitments > Scope
metadata.heading_path: Environmental commitments > Scope

content:
## Commitments

OCE commits to:

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Environmental commitments > Commitments
metadata.heading_path: Environmental commitments > Commitments

content:
## Digital-first working

OCE prioritises electronic records, signatures, communications and reporting. Printing should be avoided unless legally or operationally necessary. Digital storage, equipment and digital resources should be managed efficiently, with obsolete or duplicate data removed where appropriate and lawful.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Environmental commitments > Digital-first working
metadata.heading_path: Environmental commitments > Digital-first working

content:
## Travel

Remote participation should be considered when it can achieve the same operational purpose. When travel is necessary, staff should favour lower-emission transport, including rail over air travel where practical, combine meetings when possible and avoid unnecessary journeys.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Environmental commitments > Travel
metadata.heading_path: Environmental commitments > Travel

content:
## Procurement and equipment

When purchasing resources, OCE should consider durability, repairability, energy efficiency, expected lifespan, packaging and the supplier’s environmental practices alongside quality and operational requirements. Equipment should be reused or repaired where feasible and disposed of through appropriate recycling channels, with secure data removal.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Environmental commitments > Procurement and equipment
metadata.heading_path: Environmental commitments > Procurement and equipment

content:
## Grant-making and re-granting

For grants with potentially material environmental impacts, OCE may apply risk-based screening and request evidence of compliance with applicable environmental requirements. Environmental conditions or reporting may be included where relevant to the programme, the funded activity or donor expectations. OCE seeks to support activities that advance the Sustainable Development Goals while avoiding disproportionate administrative burdens for small or grassroots organisations.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Environmental commitments > Grant-making and re-granting
metadata.heading_path: Environmental commitments > Grant-making and re-granting

content:
## Monitoring and accountability

The Executive Director is responsible for implementation of this policy. Team members are responsible for applying it within their areas of work and reporting material concerns or non-compliance.

At least annually, OCE will review:

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Environmental commitments > Monitoring and accountability
metadata.heading_path: Environmental commitments > Monitoring and accountability

content: Any significant environmental incident connected to OCE’s direct operations must be documented and escalated to the Executive Director.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Environmental commitments
metadata.heading_path: Environmental commitments > Monitoring and accountability

content:
## Review

This policy will be reviewed at least annually. Updates will be approved by the Executive Director and communicated to the team.

metadata.heading_path: Environmental commitments > Review

## Policy

Decision confirmed by JF on 14 September 2026: OCE permits non-partisan advocacy on a cause, including advocacy concerning legislation or public policy, while excluding support for political parties or candidates. The subject of a cause alone is not grounds for exclusion. Activities must remain consistent with OCE's public-benefit purpose and applicable law.

Review the actual activity, intended use of funds, public messaging and relationships with parties, candidates or elections. If the boundary is unclear, escalate to JF for the appropriate review before accepting a commitment or applying an enforcement action. This policy decision does not constitute legal approval of every proposed activity.

Laura coordinates projects and operational follow-up; Ivan handles payment and platform operations. Project and collective communications remain with the operational team. Required financial reviews must have a designated qualified reviewer. JF resolves any gap in review coverage; this does not transfer technical validation or routine case ownership to JF.

Laura assigns an owner to every application. Ivan or an authorised substitute executes complete routine payments without systematic prior approval from CFO. Any team member may approve and execute a routine donor refund, with checks and an audit trail. CFO coordinates accounting; Laura and Ivan may participate in factual exchanges with Saïd. The owner retains responsibility for follow-up after an escalation. Responsibility for a process does not automatically confer signing authority or bank access. Reserved matters remain with the Board.

**Internal reference adopted by JF on 14 September 2026. Document owner: Laura.**

This RACI establishes operational responsibilities based on the documentation and decisions approved by JF. It replaces conflicting assignments in the August matrix for day-to-day guidance. Legal signing powers, actual access rights and external providers' engagements must still be checked against their own records. Adoption of this RACI does not certify completion of tasks.

#### 1. Agreed organisational structure

content:
Collectives and programme leads retain their programme decisions and the expense approvals specified in their agreements. The RACI below describes OCE's work; it does not transfer responsibility for all their activities to OCE.

#### 2. How to read the matrix

**A**: the person accountable for the outcome and decision within their scope. **R**: performs the work. **C**: consulted when the matter requires it. **I**: informed at the appropriate time, without prior approval.

In this matrix, CFO denotes the internal finance function. Required financial reviews must be assigned to a named, qualified person with the applicable authority. Project-facing communications remain with Laura/Ivan, including when financial advice is consulted internally.

Each row has one A. Where A also appears under R, that person owns and performs the work. Names under C do not create a mandatory approval chain. Teams receive information needed for their work, not automatically every sensitive document.

**Process ownership and individual case decisions are separate.** For example, Ivan monitors the refund queue, but any team member may decide and execute a routine refund: the case record names that person.

#### 3. Responsibility matrix

# Ask ChatGPT an operational question

**Internal guide — 14 September 2026. Owner: Laura.**

#### Before your first question

Use an authorised connection with access to the internal GitBook, if available in your ChatGPT environment. Check that ChatGPT can actually read the relevant RACI and procedure. A link alone does not prove access. Otherwise, provide current excerpts or an authorised, dated export. Do not make the handbook public to work around an access problem.

Each current team member must check connections and permissions in their own accounts. Adding these pages does not install a connection or guarantee automatic indexing. [OpenAI documentation on authorised sources and access](https://learn.chatgpt.com/es-419/docs/enterprise/chatgpt-work-cloud-security).

#### Prompt to copy

> I am \[Laura / Ivan / JF / another current role] at OCE. My case: \[situation, OCEF or OSE entity, case status, blocker and relevant deadline, without unnecessary sensitive data].
>
> Consult the OCE operational RACI adopted on 14 September 2026 and the current versions of the relevant internal procedures. Start by identifying the sources you actually read. Tell me: 1) what I should do now; 2) who performs the work and who is accountable for the decision; 3) whether I can act within the routine framework or need a decision, and from whom; 4) which documents and information are needed; 5) where to record the outcome and next action. Cite the pages and RACI rows used.
>
> Distinguish approved rules, deferred work and unresolved questions. If a source is missing or contradictory, state exactly what is missing rather than inventing a rule or authorisation. A request for advice does not authorise sending a message, making a payment or editing a document.

#### Useful examples

# CFO — budget and internal financial control

#### Scope

The CFO role focuses on OCE's budget, cash forecasts, management reporting, reliable financial figures, reconciliation review, financial controls and accounting coordination with Saïd. Its scope, deliverables and working arrangements are documented in the applicable engagement.

Financial analysis and conclusions are provided internally to the team. This role does not communicate directly with projects or collectives, manage project relationships, chase their supporting documents or act as their payment-support contact. Laura and Ivan retain the operational and project-facing responsibilities in the RACI; JF handles executive decisions and exceptions.

Ivan supplies statements, operational mappings and evidence. Saïd performs accounting work within his engagement. Laura supplies project allocations, conditions and commitments, obtains the internal financial input needed and communicates with the project or funder.

#### Financial review and continuity

Assign each required financial review to a named, qualified person with the applicable authority. Record the scope, dated conclusion, review evidence and any unresolved qualifications in the restricted case record. Refer a gap in review coverage to JF; this does not make JF the technical accounting or tax reviewer.

Existing authority for routine payments and refunds continues. Laura organises operational cover; execution requires verified access and authority. A financial validation required for a specific unresolved issue must be obtained before completing that affected action.

#### Boundaries

Financial advice does not approve a material commitment, change a funder's conditions or confer signing powers. JF and the Board retain their existing decision-making authority. Preparation and financial review remain distinct. Direct factual exchanges between Laura/Ivan and Saïd remain permitted, with accounting instructions coordinated through the designated financial reviewer.

#### Confidential references for onboarding

As part of onboarding, the CFO requests access from executive direction to the Foundation's relevant legal, tax and accounting reference documents. Review these documents with the appropriate advisers, checking their date, scope and applicability to current operations. Keep professional opinions and supporting records in restricted storage; this public handbook describes responsibilities and procedures without reproducing confidential advice.

# Documentation and pending decisions

Maintain clear guidance without turning draft policies into adopted rules.

#### Editorial standard

The public guide addresses collectives in plain, welcoming language. The internal handbook explains execution, controls, evidence and decisions. Both exclude commercial content. Keep titles short, headings consistent and one primary procedure per process.

A weekly review may correct facts, links and structure within the authorised scope. It must not invent policies or treat a proposal as approved. Preserve continuity after this initial refactor.

#### Source hierarchy

Check the applicable signed agreement and dated authorised decision first. Use operational records to establish what happened. Treat Slack, email and draft documents as supporting evidence whose authority and scope still need to be assessed.

The [professionalisation plan](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ghToLzMnkuzCyowZi0sh6aBz3jMc5RPU1uU-AOBT3Qs/edit) tracks improvement work. The [consolidated audit](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1L-xi_oBqx5osXoe_jaa4TXNSx-oZtYqA/edit) identifies direct corrections and decisions requiring validation. Editing GitBook does not itself complete a plan milestone.

#### Decisions still open in the reviewed sources

General status checked on 24 September 2026; support scope and administrative-contribution decisions updated on 19 October 2026. Operational adoption and specialist validation are separate.

content:
**Access status A07:** public, checked on 24 September 2026. The 11 September private/unpublished decision was superseded by JF’s temporary-public decision of 14 September, reconfirmed in the plan reviewed on 22 September. Keep individual case evidence, HR information and secrets in restricted systems. A sensitive unpublished change request requires an approved restricted destination before publication.

#### Administrator decision A02 — approved 14 September 2026

JF approved two genuinely active administrators by default, with a documented exception possible for a project run by one person after assessment of risk, responsibility, continuity and the expense controls. JF clarified that the sole administrator may submit and approve their own expense; OCE performs its usual pre-payment checks of supporting documents, connection to the project and applicable funding conditions, without requiring another independent approver within the collective. Record the reason, authorised decision-maker and review conditions in the existing J1-05 exceptions register. See [the administrator rule](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/application-review).

#### Payment timetable A03 — confirmed 14 September 2026

JF confirmed execution by OCE within seven business days after a submitted expense is approved by a collective administrator, with possible extension for an issue preventing payment and notification of the requester. This is an execution timeframe, not a guarantee of receipt by the beneficiary. Monday and Thursday remain usual historical processing days, not promised payment dates. See [the payment timetable](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/financial-ops-task-overview).

#### Mandate scope A04 — confirmed 14 September 2026

JF confirmed that a mandate agreement is mandatory for collectives receiving grants through OCE, optional for collectives receiving only crowdfunding donations without particular conditions, and assessed case by case for other funding arrangements. General hosting terms remain applicable. This confirms the operating scope, not legal validation of the template or signature authority. See [Prepare a mandate agreement](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures/creation-and-sending-of-mandate-agreements).

#### Administrative contributions A05 — confirmed 14 September 2026

JF confirmed the standard rates: crowdfunding through Open Collective uses an 8% administrative contribution plus actual payment-processing fees; grants and donations by bank transfer outside crowdfunding use a 10% administrative contribution. Crowdfunding costs may approximate 10% in total, but that is not a fixed all-inclusive rate.

Always obtain JF’s approval before agreeing a departure from these standard rates. Record the approved exception in the existing exceptions process. The [public fee table](https://docs.opencollective.com/oceurope/how-it-works/financial-contributions-how-to-donate#administrative-contributions) is the reference for standard rates; link to it rather than maintaining competing tables. The support framework and calculation rules under J2-03 were approved for integration on 19 October 2026; use [Forms of support and administrative contributions](/oc-europe-internal-doc/the-foundation/forms-of-support-and-administrative-contributions). Actual cost reviews and contractual/tax implementation remain separate.

#### Grant tracking A06 — scoped for the next cycle, 14 September 2026

The work allocation confirmed on 14 September 2026 remains the basis for J2-02: Open Collective provides the register of funds and collectives, while the dedicated application covers complementary operational grant tracking. Laura defines the process, information to track, channels, responsibilities, constraints and needs not covered by Open Collective; she may use ChatGPT to help prepare the diagram. JF builds the application from that architecture.

The application is now available and functional validation remains in progress. See [Tools and records — grant tracking](/oc-europe-internal-doc/tools-and-platforms-used-at-oce#grant-tracking-next-cycle-delivery) for the dated implementation status and J2-02 target. For submitted Myriad requests, follow the recording step in [Coordinate Myriad USA](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures/myriad-usa). Keep supporting evidence linked and reuse existing records without creating a competing master list.

The grant-tracking responsibility and delivery sequence are decided; functional validation remains under the existing J2-02 task. Other tool and financial-system mapping validations remain separate.

#### Currency conversion A08 — approved 14 September 2026

When incoming funds are in a different currency from the collective, execute an actual conversion into the collective’s currency when processing the receipt, in either direction, including USD to EUR and EUR to USD. Credit the collective with the net amount actually obtained from the executed conversion, not a notional amount calculated from an indicative daily rate. The collective bears the conversion costs included in that operation; do not deduct those same costs a second time. Retain the conversion evidence, including the date, applied rate, source amount and net amount received.

JF approved this incoming-funds rule. The wider foreign-exchange risk policy under J3-06 remains a separate financial workstream. See [incoming bank transfers](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/bank-transfers-for-the-collectives).

#### Public funding A09 — decision confirmed 14 September 2026

JF confirmed on 14 September 2026 that OCE has not yet accepted public funding. Public funding remains an exploratory opportunity for hosted collectives and for OCE itself, with previous exploration involving Open Source Europe. Assess each opportunity individually; this is not an established form of support or a blanket eligibility commitment. JF gives the go-ahead before OCE commits to a case. Review the funder’s conditions and the applicable legal arrangement for that opportunity.

See [Receive European funding](/oc-europe-internal-doc/grantmaking-procedures/receiving-funds-from-europe). This decision defines the approval route; it does not approve a particular grant or settle tax and legal validations.

#### Application follow-up A11 — approved 14 September 2026

JF approved a first response from the team within seven business days of receiving an application. This is not a deadline for the final acceptance decision. Further discussion, information requests, reminders and closure are assessed case by case, without an automatic closure deadline. See [Review an application](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/application-review).

#### Platform tips D11 — confirmed 14 September 2026

JF confirmed that platform tips support Ofico’s maintenance of the Open Collective platform, rather than OCE. Tips are distinct from OCE’s administrative contribution. Tips remain enabled at host level and no individual collective may obtain an exception to that setting. This does not make tipping mandatory for donors: each donor may change the tip amount or set it to zero at checkout. Do not apply the administrative-fee exception process to waive this host-level rule.

#### Professionalisation links

J1-06 covers contradictory documentation. J1-02 covers access; J1-03 covers delegations; J1-05 covers genuine exceptions. The financial pack, continuity test and risk policies remain work to evidence, not capabilities to claim as completed. The complementary grant-tracking application is available; its functional validation remains in progress under J2-02 as described above.

#### Release checklist

Read the current pages; isolate a change request; preserve third-party work; verify content, links and audience; merge the authorised changes; reread the final pages and record the revision. Keep old URLs working after moves. Record unresolved items with the competent validator rather than repeating warnings everywhere.

#### Confidentiality

No private source text, unpublished facts, case names or private URLs go into the external guide. The internal guide may explain confirmed professional procedures, while sensitive case files, credentials and authentication links stay in their restricted systems.

#### Source and review

Editorial consistency review: 24 September 2026, following JF’s instruction. Sources: current GitBook revisions, adopted decisions of 14 September, [plan reviewed on 22 September](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ghToLzMnkuzCyowZi0sh6aBz3jMc5RPU1uU-AOBT3Qs/edit) and [published hosting template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/e/2PACX-1vS2jTb55T-kXHDPLNWVg4xUuMGmediT9VBqwsNpdQA8geRpcPsyYvfPggwJ6iZaPw/pub). The corrections do not certify outstanding legal/tax validations or implementation of every operational control.

#### First-triage decision confirmed — 14 September 2026

JF confirmed on 14 September 2026 that the team had agreed the following routing the previous week: Laura reviews all incoming applications first, then routes each one to herself, Ivan, or Lucas. The Lucas route applies when an open-source project has applied to the wrong host and should apply to Open Source Europe. The exact date of the earlier discussion was not specified. This confirmation concerns first triage only; other audit decisions and specialist validations remain unchanged.

#### Operational responsibility reference — 14 September 2026

Use the [RACI adopted on 14 September 2026](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/raci-operationnelle) and [current-source question guide](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/question-chatgpt). Signing powers, access and specialist validations remain separate.

#### Final consistency pass — 24 September 2026

JF requested correction of the audit findings. Editorial corrections implement existing decisions; they do not amend signed agreements or appoint new decision-makers.

metadata.heading_path: Documentation and pending decisions > Decisions still open in the reviewed sources

content:
These items belong to the existing J1-06 reliquat and related plan tasks, not a new parallel register. Dates remain those in the [current plan](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ghToLzMnkuzCyowZi0sh6aBz3jMc5RPU1uU-AOBT3Qs/edit); no new deadline is adopted here.

**Drafting direction for contract alignment — not an amendment:** use the mandate scope in this page (mandatory for grants, optional for unconditional crowdfunding, other arrangements case by case) and the adopted advocacy policy (non-partisan advocacy permitted; party/candidate support excluded). Preserve applicable-law, funder-restriction and notice requirements. Publication of this note does not alter an initiative’s signed agreement.

**Maintenance:** Laura is the documentation owner under the adopted role model. Keep one procedure per process and link its dated decision. Review after a rule/tool change and at the existing plan review. Old GitBook drafts must be compared with the live revision before any merge; preserve other authors’ work and do not merge sensitive guidance into this public space.

#### Support framework and contribution calculations — approved 19 October 2026

JF authorised integration of the consolidated framework into this handbook on 19 October 2026. [Forms of support and administrative contributions](/oc-europe-internal-doc/the-foundation/forms-of-support-and-administrative-contributions) is the operating reference for the three forms of support, included scope, funding classification, default calculation base, intermediary costs, internal transfers, cancellation adjustments and programme costing. Standard rates remain those adopted on 14 September; existing particular agreements and amendments remain applicable.

A documented bank transfer within the Open Collective crowdfunding journey may be classified as crowdfunding. A grant remains a grant regardless of payment method. The page defines the evidence required and the treatment of existing agreements. The previous open policy question on this boundary is resolved; alignment of templates and external wording remains implementation work.

No partner-specific rate, universal programme minimum, interest allocation or tax conclusion is created by this approval. New particular contributions still follow the existing decision authority. Operational adoption does not certify current programme profitability or settle outstanding financial reconciliations. Keep negotiated case terms and private evidence outside this public handbook.

**Terminology — confirmed by JF on 19 October 2026:** describe the Foundation's activities as forms of support, hosting, fund administration and administrative contributions. Use this vocabulary consistently in titles, guidance and communications.

Challenge reasoning, minimise data and verify outputs before relying on them.

AI can help draft, organise, compare and question information. The person responsible for the work remains accountable for the result.

content:
## Use it as a sparring partner

For strategic or complex work, ask it to examine assumptions, identify counterarguments, test the reasoning, propose alternatives and distinguish facts from uncertainty. The objective is better judgement, not automatic agreement.

metadata.heading_path: Use AI responsibly > Use it as a sparring partner

content:
## Select tools and context carefully

Use an authorised account and tools appropriate to the data. A connector being available does not mean it should receive an entire mailbox or folder. Retrieve only the professional material needed for the task.

Do not supply passwords, recovery codes, authentication links or unnecessary personal data. Keep individual safeguarding, HR and beneficiary records out of reusable prompts and documentation. Reduce or anonymise details when they are not needed.

metadata.heading_path: Use AI responsibly > Select tools and context carefully

Review important outgoing messages before sending them. For documentation, the approved scope can authorise direct editorial changes, but does not approve new substantive policy. No message to a third party should be sent merely because it appears as a next step in an AI output.

# Forms of support and administrative contributions > Choose the form of support
Arrangement: A support fund for an existing organisation.
OCE's role: Receive and allocate funding intended for an independent organisation, control onward transfers and follow the agreed obligations.
Scope to establish: Identify the recipient, purpose, agreement, authorised transfers and reporting. The organisation remains independent; this is not unrestricted banking or automatic pass-through.

# OCE operational RACI > 1. Agreed organisational structure
Person: **JF — executive direction**.
Main responsibility: Strategy, budget and resources, major partnerships, policies, exceptions and material decisions; relationship with the Board.
Key boundary: Does not become the routine case manager merely by making a decision on it.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: OCE operational RACI > 1. Agreed organisational structure

content:
# OCE operational RACI > 1. Agreed organisational structure
Person: **Laura — operational coordination and projects**.
Main responsibility: Triage of all applications, admission within the established framework, allocation of work, complex funds, funder commitments and reports, risk and procedure follow-up.
Key boundary: Does not approve accounting or tax treatment in the competent financial reviewer's place; cannot independently extend a material commitment.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: OCE operational RACI > 1. Agreed organisational structure

content:
# OCE operational RACI > 1. Agreed organisational structure
Person: **Ivan — financial and platform operations**.
Main responsibility: First-level checks, routine payments, allocation of identified receipts, support, delegated onboarding, records and access.
Key boundary: Does not independently certify reconciliations or figures he prepares; does not decide a legal model or a substantial exception.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: OCE operational RACI > 1. Agreed organisational structure

content:
# OCE operational RACI > 1. Agreed organisational structure
Person: **CFO**.
Main responsibility: Reliable figures, reconciliations, financial review, budget and forecasts, control of fund flows, coordination with Saïd and financial advice.
Key boundary: Internal budget and finance role only; no direct contact with projects or collectives. Not a routine payment gate.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: OCE operational RACI > 1. Agreed organisational structure

content:
# OCE operational RACI > 1. Agreed organisational structure
Person: **Saïd — accountant**.
Main responsibility: Bookkeeping, preparation of returns and accounts, technical advice within his engagement.
Key boundary: His scope depends on his actual engagement; the RACI does not automatically assign certification or an external audit.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: OCE operational RACI > 1. Agreed organisational structure

content:
# OCE operational RACI > 1. Agreed organisational structure
Person: **Board**.
Main responsibility: Reserved governance decisions, oversight of executive direction, alternative route for conflicts involving JF.
Key boundary: Does not approve routine actions. Actual powers remain those of the applicable governance framework.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: OCE operational RACI > 1. Agreed organisational structure

content:
# OCE operational RACI > 1. Agreed organisational structure
Person: **Lucas — Open Source Europe liaison**.
Main responsibility: Receives open-source projects referred to OSE by Laura.
Key boundary: Does not approve OCEF operations; OSE admission and operations fall under OSE's own organisation.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: OCE operational RACI > 1. Agreed organisational structure
